title: How a Rice Cooker Works in 60 Seconds 🍚🧲 #shorts
description:
A simple rice cooker knows when rice is done using physics, not a timer. While water is left, the pot can't go above 100°C. Once the water is absorbed, the temperature climbs, a magnet in the thermostat loses its pull, and the cooker drops to warm. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#ricecooker #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A basic rice cooker has *no timer*. It uses a *magnet* to know when rice is done.

steps.label: Heater
steps.text: Press the switch, and a *heating plate* under the inner pot gets very hot.

steps.label: Boiling
steps.text: Water can't get hotter than *100°C* while it boils, so the pot stays stuck there.

steps.label: Absorbed
steps.text: The rice *soaks up* the water. With no water left, the pot finally climbs past 100°C.

steps.label: Magnet
steps.text: A magnet in the thermostat *loses its pull* when it gets that hot, and lets go.

steps.label: Click
steps.text: A spring snaps the switch with a *click*, and the cooker drops to *keep warm*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Boil, absorb, *click*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
